quote: I’m almost 37 weeks, and a FTM, I feel like I’m doing a good job preparing myself and being meticulous from using community resources, researching, getting a doula. I don’t have family nearby but have made good friends that live a few blocks in all directions.
cx: How she has prepared before her mother-in-law's visit was booked.

quote: mother in law, though she said it’s whatever we want - towards her son said that she wants to hold baby after him, and this is her heir how could she not be there at delivery, and that we were telling her to come later in August like 08/03-08/10 cause we didn’t want her there. And a whole bunch of stuff, so he booked her flight for 7/29.
cx: Her mother-in-law flies in from across the country three days before the due date, booked by her husband.

quote: I feel like I have lost control over a moment I had in my mind. […] I’m nervous of going into labor and my partner being called on by his mother.
cx: What the flight booking took from her picture of the birth.

quote: I’m just hoping I deliver before they get here and avoid it all together. I think I’ve decided at least no visitors for 24 hours after birth and want my partner there with me fully for us to bond over becoming a mom and dad.
cx: Her fallback plan once the mother-in-law's arrival date was fixed.

quote: we are first time parents and don’t know what to expect during labor and pp, and what we should be aware of in terms of boundaries, rules, tips or tricks that might help a mother who’s not to keen on emotional people being in their space during this very vulnerable time.
cx: What she asks strangers for, days before the due date.

quote: Throughout my pregnancy, she has started pushing back on many of our parenting decisions before the baby is even born. Things like newborn kissing, safe sleep, the type of learning we want for our daughter, and even what she should wear for her baptism.
cx: First-time mother who had asked her mother-in-law to provide part-time childcare after leave.

quote: I started touring daycares. I honestly fell in love with one. The infant room was wonderful, the teachers were so warm, and I left feeling much more excited about daycare than I ever expected.
cx: Touring daycares while pregnant, for a return to work at five months.

quote: I feel guilty because she’ll only be around 5 months old when she starts, even though she’d only be going 2 days a week. […] We can afford it, things would change with our budget which makes me nervous but it may be worth cutting back on other expenses for this peace of mind.
cx: Weighing paid daycare against free grandparent care.

quote: My fear is that I’ll be taken off guard when it happens and be overwhelmed physically by anxiety; so I have times where I’m doing other normal life stuff now and have a moment of freaking out like “What if it happened now you weren’t thinking about it”.
cx: A father-to-be in the last days before the due date.

quote: I feel bad when asked “But are you excited?” and I really can only point to things that mostly occur later in our childs life as opposed to the birth, newborn, baby stage that I currently see as just a huge challenge.
cx: Same father on his wife's question.

quote:
Instead, she started repeatedly saying, “She’s just on her period.”  
I didn’t even respond because I was honestly shocked she was saying that while I’m pregnant. My mom finally said, “She isn’t on her period. She’s pregnant.”
cx: 32 weeks; a family day out where her sister needles her.

quote:
Now that I’m the pregnant one, I feel like I’m constantly walking on eggshells around her.  
Am I overthinking this because I’m pregnant, or does this actually sound like resentment?
cx: Same post, asking strangers whether pregnancy is colouring her view.

quote: I was going to make a social media post for my friends and family to inform them of my decision to give them plenty of time to decide whether or not they want to get vaccinated before baby arrives, but I didn’t want to come off as an AH for announcing it.
cx: Planning how to announce her visitor rule in advance.

quote: So tell me why mothers who choose unmedicated, low intervention births are still regularly bombarded with replies telling them they are "trying too hard" and that "they aren't impressing anyone" and other unsolicited opinions that are completely unhelpful?
cx: A pregnant birthworker on how forums answer women planning low-intervention births.

quote: I still do all the chores I did before and work full time.  Still meal plan, grocery shop, laundry, clean house, vacuum, take care of dog, garden, dust, mop, change linens, clean bathrooms.  He works long hours and is completely dedicated to his job while he is there.
cx: 35 weeks, first baby, an easy pregnancy until now.

quote: I'm hitting a wall. My ankles are swollen all the time.  Feet and back hurt.  Insomnia.  Get tired easily.  Can't bend over to tie my shoes.  I need some help and support.
cx: The week the easy pregnancy stopped being easy.

quote: I can guilt him in to a half hearted foot rub on occasion, but I end up feeling bad for imposing on him. It doesn't occur to him to relieve me of any of this load or do something extra.  So my requests for specific tasks are beginning to feel needy and nagging.
cx: Same post: asking her partner for help.

quote: I certainly don't want the expectation that his life postpartum will carry on as before, just with a baby to cuddle when he feels like it.
cx: What she fears about the weeks after the birth.

quote: we were talking with some people teasing about how my husband is prone to fainting and she said I’ll catch you and he said you won’t be there, and she said “yes I will”….she was there when I invited her mom so I thought I was clear.
cx: Six weeks to go; her sister-in-law plans to be at the birth uninvited.

quote: I’m working on a way to nicely\*\*\*say that I just want mom and MIL there and nobody else. Whenever I think of how to word it, it comes across as mean…
cx: Trying to word her hospital-visitor rule for her husband's family.
